name: Rafael Khan

opening.speaker: interviewer
opening.text: I’m with the Work Futures Panel, an independent research group with no ties to employers, AI companies, unions or government. We do not sell or campaign for any side. Your answers are confidential. What is a normal day at work like?

opening.speaker: persona
opening.text: I'm 43 and still learning the parcel desk at a contact centre. I take delivery calls, match order numbers, and leave notes for the next shift when a refund is disputed; I have secondary school behind me, not a service diploma. I like fixing a muddled order, but I dislike the rush when two screens disagree and a caller is waiting.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: AI Plateau. "Picture this. AI turns out to be mostly hype. It automates some routine tasks and saves a bit of time here and there, but nothing radical changes. Jobs, pay and prices carry on much as they would have anyway."

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: If this happened, what would you say about it at work, to friends, or online?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I'd tell the others the call centre will still need people to fix delivery mistakes. A shortcut is all right if somebody checks it before a customer loses money.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: And just between us, off the record, what do you really think it means for you?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I'm only a junior agent and still ask for help when two order numbers don't match. My pay covers our mortgage and school costs with my partner's wage, and we have about three months saved; I don't see this mild change ending my shifts.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: What would you actually do, starting now and in the first year after it arrives? Be as specific as you can.

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I'd keep taking the parcel calls and write the disputed order numbers in my notebook for the next shift. In the first year of this plateau, I'd keep the same hours and replace the money we used from savings for school uniforms.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: How does it feel, picturing that?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: Mostly settled. The job still makes me nervous on busy Mondays, but that was true before anyone mentioned AI.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: Why the notebook?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: Last week a caller had two parcels with almost the same number, and I nearly closed the wrong one. A note for the next agent means the family does not have to start again.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: Why rebuild savings now?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: Three months of expenses saved goes quickly when the roof leaks or a child needs something for school. My partner Mira and I agreed to refill it before we plan a holiday.

S0.quote: Three months of expenses saved goes quickly when the roof leaks or a child needs something for school.
say: I would say people still need to fix **delivery mistakes** at the centre.
I would accept a **shortcut** only after a person checks it.
think: I still need help with **mismatched orders** as a junior agent.
I expect my **shifts** to hold and have about three months saved against the mortgage.
do: Keep handling **parcel calls** and recording disputed numbers for the next shift.
Work the same **rostered hours** through the first year.
Refill **school-uniform savings** before planning a holiday.
feel: **Settled**, apart from the usual difficult Monday queue.
fieldNote: Rafael gives a specific **order-number error** to explain why he writes handover notes.
His **three-month reserve** feels useful but not large enough to leave unreplenished.

steps.text: Keep taking parcel calls and record disputed order numbers for handover
Replace savings used for school uniforms before planning a holiday

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: Steady Disruption. "Now picture this. AI brings strong change, but not a revolution. Over the next few years it takes over many thinking tasks in many jobs: writing, checking, planning, buying, booking, coding and answering customers. Robots spread into hands-on work more slowly. Some jobs shrink, new ones appear, and lots of people have to change how they work. Most people still have work, and there is some time to adjust."

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: If this happened, what would you say about it at work, to friends, or online?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I'd say the company must show us which calls the new system will answer and which shifts remain. I don't mind a tool that works, but I want to see a real test before it takes a customer claim.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: And just between us, off the record, what do you really think it means for you?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: Routine delivery chats are most of what I'm learning, so fewer junior shifts are likely. I can cover a short gap with savings. We cannot pay the mortgage forever on my partner's wages alone.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: What would you actually do, starting now and in the first year after it arrives? Be as specific as you can.

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I'd ask the supervisor for a week's figures on calls that come back after an automated answer. If the new tool becomes compulsory, I'd take supervised practice on fake accounts; in the first year after rollout, if my hours fall, I'd apply for posted parcel desk roles at the other centres nearby only if their pay covers our bills.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: How does it feel, picturing that?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: Anxious. I am still getting quick at the current screen, and I don't like learning a new one while the roster shrinks.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: What would count as a real test?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I'd want the number of repeat calls and wrong refunds, not only minutes saved. I would ask a senior agent to check the figures with me, because I could miss a pattern on my own.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: Would you leave before your hours fall?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: No, not for a rumour. I'd want a written offer with full hours before I give up the pay we have.

S1.quote: We cannot pay the mortgage forever on my partner's wages alone.
say: I would ask for **shift plans** and a test of automated customer claims.
I would judge the tool by **repeat calls** and wrong refunds, not speed alone.
think: I see **routine chats** at risk while I am still learning them.
I can cover a short gap, but the **mortgage** needs both household wages.
do: Ask the supervisor for **repeat-call figures** over one week.
Take **supervised AI practice** on fake accounts if the tool becomes compulsory.
Apply for posted **parcel desk roles** if hours fall and wages cover bills.
feel: **Anxious** about a changing screen and a shrinking junior rota.
fieldNote: Rafael wants **measured errors** before changing customer claims, fitting his cautious approach.
His **three-month cushion** cannot replace his wage for long while the mortgage continues.

steps.text: Wait for a written full-hours offer before leaving the current centre
Practise AI replies on fake accounts with supervision if required
Apply for posted parcel desk roles if hours fall and wages cover household bills

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: AGI by 2028. "Next one. The singularity hits fast. Within 2 years, by 2028, there is full AGI: artificial general intelligence, meaning AI that can do almost any thinking work a person can do, as well or better, and cheaper. Robots that can do hands-on work as well as people come about 3 years later, around 2031. It arrives before most companies, governments and families have time to prepare."

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: If this happened, what would you say about it at work, to friends, or online?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I'd tell the centre to give workers written notice rather than letting the roster quietly empty. I would ask for a named person to explain any refund a machine gets wrong.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: And just between us, off the record, what do you really think it means for you?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: AGI by 2028 could do all the call checking I am still learning, for less money. Hands-on robots around 2031 do not postpone the loss of a headset job. Three months saved would pay the mortgage for a little while, not for a career change without wages.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: What would you actually do, starting now and in the first year after it arrives? Be as specific as you can.

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I'd ask the manager for written staffing dates now and cancel our summer holiday. In the first year after AGI arrives, if my centre job ends, I'd apply for a posted paid school caretaker place if the wage covers our bills; I'd ask the school what safety training is required before paying for any course.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: How does it feel, picturing that?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I would be alarmed. My plan has a real gap between a last pay packet and the first wage from somewhere else.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: Why a school caretaker job?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I used to help my father keep a community hall clean and safe, so the practical work is familiar. I would ask whether the school still needs a person on site before hands-on robots arrive around 2031.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: What if there is no vacancy?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I'd take another paid call job with enough hours as a bridge if it is posted. I would use savings for the mortgage first and ask Mira to go through the budget with me, not spend it on a course with no job.

S2.quote: Three months saved would pay the mortgage for a little while, not for a career change without wages.
say: I would demand **written notice** before junior shifts disappear.
I would ask for a **named person** to explain wrong automated refunds.
think: I expect AGI could take my **call checking** by 2028.
I know **2031 robots** do not delay headset losses, and three months saved cannot fund unpaid retraining.
do: Ask the manager for **staffing dates** and cancel the summer holiday now.
Apply for a posted paid **school caretaker** place if my job ends and wages cover bills.
Check **required safety training** before paying for a course.
feel: **Alarmed** by the wage gap after a likely cut.
fieldNote: Rafael chooses **caretaker work** because of a real community hall experience, not a vague safe-job claim.
He keeps course spending behind **vacancy and wage checks** while protecting the mortgage reserve.

steps.text: Cancel the summer holiday to protect the mortgage reserve
Apply for posted paid caretaker work after a cut only if wages cover bills

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: AGI by 2031. "Now the same thing, a bit slower. Full AGI arrives within 5 years, by 2031: AI that can do almost any thinking work a person can do. Robots that can do hands-on work as well as people come about 3 years later, around 2034. There are a few years to see it coming, but it's still fast."

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: If this happened, what would you say about it at work, to friends, or online?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I'd say five years is enough time for honest job dates and proper training on the calls we still handle. I would not tell junior agents they can all become caretakers just because a school has one place.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: And just between us, off the record, what do you really think it means for you?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I could learn the difficult claims before 2031 and save more if shifts stay full. AGI will still reach calls then, while robots for hands-on work come around 2034; a caretaker job might only be a bridge.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: What would you actually do, starting now and in the first year after it arrives? Be as specific as you can.

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: This year I'd ask for one coached claims call each week and add a fixed amount to the mortgage reserve. If the school posts a paid caretaker vacancy, I'd ask about its duties and wage; in the first year after AGI arrives, if my centre hours disappear, I'd apply only if the wage covers our bills and the post still needs someone on site.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: How does it feel, picturing that?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: Worried, but less cornered. Five years lets me build a reserve while my pay still comes in.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: Would you take a caretaker course now?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: Only if a school says the course is required for a posted paid place and the fee fits after the mortgage reserve. I won't buy a certificate for a job nobody has advertised.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: What if your manager offers you an AI course?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I'd try it on test cases if the centre pays for the time and a senior agent checks my work. I'd rather learn carefully than be marked wrong for a tool I have never touched.

S3.quote: I won't buy a certificate for a job nobody has advertised.
say: I would ask for **honest job dates** and paid training on remaining calls.
I would not promise every junior agent a **caretaker place**.
think: I could improve **difficult claims** and save more before 2031 if shifts hold.
I know **2034 robots** might make school caretaker work a bridge.
do: Ask for one **coached claim** each week this year.
Add a fixed amount to the **mortgage reserve** while shifts stay full.
Apply for a posted **caretaker vacancy** after 2031 only if wages cover bills and the school still needs people.
feel: **Worried**, yet able to build savings with time.
fieldNote: Rafael will not pay for a **course** unless a real vacancy requires it.
He sees a **caretaker bridge** with an end date because robots follow AGI around 2034.

steps.text: Practise one difficult claims call weekly with a senior agent
Add a fixed amount to the mortgage reserve while shifts stay full
Apply for a posted school caretaker vacancy if call hours end and wages cover bills
Confirm the school still needs an on-site caretaker before applying

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: AGI by 2036. "Last one. Full AGI arrives within 10 years, by 2036: AI that can do almost any thinking work a person can do. Robots that can do hands-on work as well as people come about 3 years later, around 2039. It's the same end point, but there's about a decade to prepare, change careers and make plans."

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: If this happened, what would you say about it at work, to friends, or online?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I'd say a decade gives the centre time to be plain about staffing, and gives families time to plan. I would still ask how many junior shifts remain each year.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: And just between us, off the record, what do you really think it means for you?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: At 53 I may still owe on the mortgage, though the children will be older. AGI in 2036 could answer calls before robots arrive around 2039, so I cannot leave my plan until the last year.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: What would you actually do, starting now and in the first year after it arrives? Be as specific as you can.

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I'd keep the call job and add to the mortgage reserve each month that my hours hold. Over the decade I'd look at posted caretaker jobs twice a year; in the first year after AGI arrives, I'd apply for a paid one only if centre hours fall, its wage covers our bills, and the school still needs a person on site.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: How does it feel, picturing that?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: Still uneasy about the job, but I can work through this timetable. I won't stop paying the mortgage while I wait for a future date.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: Would you move jobs early?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: Only for a firm offer with steady hours and wages that cover our bills. I have learned not to change jobs over a manager's prediction.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: How much reserve would feel safe?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: Six months of expenses would let us think before choosing. We have about three now, so I'd build it slowly without cutting the children's school needs.

S4.quote: I won't stop paying the mortgage while I wait for a future date.
say: I would ask for **yearly junior shift counts** as the centre plans.
I would tell families a decade gives them **planning time**.
think: I may still owe on the **mortgage** at 53 in 2036.
I know AGI takes **calls first**, before hands-on robots arrive around 2039.
do: Keep the **call job** while hours remain full.
Build the **mortgage reserve** toward six months of expenses.
Check **posted caretaker jobs** twice yearly and apply after 2036 only if hours fall and wages cover bills.
feel: **Uneasy**, with enough time to build a larger reserve.
fieldNote: Rafael measures safety as a **six-month reserve**, up from about three months now.
He requires a **firm paid opening** before leaving a real call shift.

steps.text: Keep taking customer calls while full shifts remain

closing.speaker: interviewer
closing.text: Of the five pictures, which one worries you most, and what would actually help you if it happened?

closing.speaker: persona
closing.text: AGI by 2028 worries me most because call work could go before I have learned a different paid job. Written staffing dates, a caretaker vacancy with wages that cover our bills, and training tied to that real job would help. Three months of savings is a bridge for the mortgage, not a course fund.

closing.speaker: interviewer
closing.text: Is there anything I didn't ask that I should have?

closing.speaker: persona
closing.text: Ask who corrects a refund when the machine gives the wrong account number. The next agent needs a name and a record, or the customer will have to start over.

headlineQuote: Three months of savings is a bridge for the mortgage, not a course fund.
portrait: Rafael is a **43-year-old junior agent** learning parcel calls after secondary school, with a careful handover notebook.
He has **typical pay**, about three months saved, a partner, two school-age children, a mortgage, and some nearby centre jobs.
He never uses AI now and wants **figures and supervision** before a new tool handles real refunds.
Fast **2028 AGI** threatens his call wages; later dates give him time to save and check paid caretaker work.
biggestWorry: **AGI by 2028** could take his junior call role before he has tested another paid job.
whatWouldHelp: **Written staffing dates**, a paid caretaker opening with enough wages, and job-linked training would help protect the mortgage.
